sections.title: Bringing the second half of Unit 23 together
sections.content: lehet + infinitive (never conjugated) asks or states what's generally possible: Lehet itt parkolni? – Igen, lehet. szabad + infinitive (also never conjugated) states what a rule allows: Szabad itt dohányozni? – Nem, nem szabad. nem szabad is a strong prohibition, closer to "must not" than a soft "can't". Fold either idea into one word with -hat/-het attached to the verb: mehetek ("I may/can go") is a shorter way of saying Lehet mennem.

sections.title: Three kinds of "can", side by side
rows: Today it's possible to swim in the lake. (the situation)
I may/can go — one word or two

items.english: Is it possible to take photos in the spa?

items.spanish: A kórházban nem szabad dohányozni, ez szigorú szabály.
items.english: You must not smoke in the hospital — it's a strict rule.

items.spanish: Mit tudunk ma csinálni? Biciklizhetünk, vagy horgászhatunk a tónál.
items.english: What can we do today? We could cycle, or fish by the lake.

items.spanish: Itt dohányozhatsz, de a kórházban nem.
items.english: You can smoke here, but not in the hospital.

sections.content: A quick way to choose: yours personally → tud. The circumstances → lehet. A rule someone wrote down → szabad. When all three line up, the plan actually works.
